report_name: Coinkite Coldcard Firmware Flaw Enables $100M+ Bitcoin Heist

threat_actors.name: Unnamed Hacking Groups
threat_actors.description: Multiple, distinct hacking groups that exploited a firmware vulnerability in Coinkite Coldcard hardware wallets to brute-force private keys and steal over $100 million in Bitcoin.
threat_actors.goals: Financial theft of Bitcoin by guessing private keys of vulnerable wallets.

attack_patterns.name: Brute Force
attack_patterns.description: Attackers systematically generated private keys to find wallets with a balance, exploiting a weak pseudorandom number generator in the device firmware that reduced the key space entropy from 128 bits to as low as 40 bits.

vulnerabilities.name: Coldcard Weak PRNG Firmware Vulnerability
vulnerabilities.description: A build configuration error in Coinkite Coldcard firmware released between March 2021 and July 2026 caused the device to fall back from a hardware entropy source to a weak software-based pseudorandom number generator (PRNG). This reduced the seed phrase entropy from 128 bits to as low as 40 bits, allowing private keys to be guessed via brute force.

identities.name: Coinkite
identities.description: Vendor of the Coldcard hardware wallet whose firmware contained a critical vulnerability leading to the mass theft of Bitcoin.

identities.name: Federal Investigators
identities.description: A class of high-profile victims whose Bitcoin, stored on vulnerable Coldcard wallets, was stolen.
